question: As the number of days grows, do class-tagged memory intervals shrink at the parametric rate while price-only intervals do not, so that the advantage of tagging grows with the sample, as Theorem discvalue predicts?
honesty_note: No public data tag order flow by trader at the level Proposition tagged assumes. The closest public analogue, Binance class-level positions, is what Chapter 2 already uses; this test checks a new scaling prediction on new days with the same estimators, not a new kind of data.
freshness: No 2025-2026 file of the repository that mentions these symbols uses the 7th, 21st or 30th of a month, except 2025-04-07, 2026-07-21 and 2026-09-30, which are excluded; the dates are disjoint from those of E1v2 (4th, 5th, 18th, 19th, 23rd) and G1 (8th, 29th, 31st).
estimators: Paper 1 estimators as registered with E1v2 (five_min, tagged_fit, kernel_fit), day bootstrap with 150 draws
subsamples: one random permutation of each symbol's valid days (seed 20261025 + 37 x symbol index); nested subsamples of the first 14, the first 28 and all valid days

per_symbol.s_tag: OLS slope of log(mean class-tagged rate-interval width) on log n
per_symbol.s_ratio: OLS slope of log(width_price / width_tag) on log n

primary_1: P1 holds in at least 75% of evaluable symbols and its Holm-adjusted one-sided binomial p (null 1/2) is below 0.05
primary_2: P2 holds in at least 75% of evaluable symbols and its Holm-adjusted one-sided binomial p (null 1/2) is below 0.05
evaluable: at least 40 valid days; void if fewer than 20 symbols are evaluable
what_is_mechanical: P1 partly reflects ordinary regression behaviour and P2 partly the bounded range of the price-only rate intervals. The informative failures are a tagged slope far from -1/2 (non-stationary class memory) and a ratio that does not grow (price-only identification improving with data as fast as tagged).
opening_rule: Specification, hash and counter at 0 are pushed in a commit of their own before any of these files is downloaded; the pipeline refuses to run unless the committed specification matches and the counter is 0; it sets the counter to 1 and evaluates once.
